name: rt_restore_ucontext
prose: Static inline function taking regs, sw and a user ucontext pointer uc; it restores the register context from uc. It first sets current->restart_block.fn to do_no_restart_syscall. It reads uc->uc_mcontext.version into temp with __get_user, accumulating the error in err but not testing err yet; if temp != MCONTEXT_VERSION it returns -1 at once with regs and sw untouched (temp is whatever it held if the read failed). Otherwise it reads the registers from gregs: regs->d0..d5, sw->d6, sw->d7, regs->a0..a2, sw->a3..a6, the user stack pointer (written with wrusp(usp) even if an earlier read failed), regs->pc, and gregs[17], from which only the low byte replaces the low byte of regs->sr; it sets regs->orig_d0 to -1; it reads uc->uc_formatvec into temp; and calls rt_restore_fpu_state(uc) and restore_altstack(&uc->uc_stack), ORing their results into err. If err is non-zero it returns -1 (regs, sw and the user stack pointer may already have been changed). Otherwise it returns mangle_kernel_stack(regs, temp, &uc->uc_extra), which returns -1 if the frame format has no valid extra size or copying the extra frame from user space fails (before setting anything), and otherwise sets regs->format and regs->vector, moves the kernel stack frame down by the extra size when it is non-zero (updating current->thread.esp0) and returns the extra size (zero or positive).
note: Reviewers original/round 2/round 15 all point at paths the old prose already listed (-1 for altstack, FPU, version) except round 15, which is partly right: the read error of the version word does not return by itself (signal.c slice 214-216); it only matters via err at the end, which is now stated. Slice cut the tail of mangle_kernel_stack; read from the real file (signal.c:644-681).

name: q40_platform_init
prose: Static __init function with no arguments, registered with arch_initcall. If MACH_IS_Q40 is false it returns -ENODEV (-19) without registering anything. Otherwise it calls platform_device_register_simple for "q40kbd" (id -1, no resources) and for "atari-falcon-ide" with id 0 and q40_pata_rsrc_0 and with id 1 and q40_pata_rsrc_1, ignoring the return values (a failed registration is not reported), and then returns 0. The only returns are -ENODEV and 0.
note: Contract cleared: it depends on the machine global and registers devices, and the old ensures was too weak (reviewer round 15 right: it did not tie -19 to the non-Q40 case). Prose precondition about locks removed as unsupported. Slice 39-54.

name: SYSCALL_DEFINE6(mmap, unsigned long, addr, unsigned long, len, unsigned long, prot, unsigned long, flags, unsigned long, fd, unsigned long, pgoff)
prose: Generated microblaze syscall function sys_mmap taking addr, len, prot, flags, fd and pgoff, where pgoff here is a byte offset. If (pgoff & ~PAGE_MASK) is non-zero, i.e. the offset is not a multiple of the page size, it returns -EINVAL and calls nothing else. Otherwise it returns the value of ksys_mmap_pgoff(addr, len, prot, flags, fd, pgoff >> PAGE_SHIFT) unchanged. Those are its only two returns.
note: Macro-generated function; name is the SYSCALL_DEFINE6 invocation (sys_microblaze.c:36-44). Old prose accurate; the sentence about caller references was dropped as unsupported by the code.

name: SYSCALL_DEFINE6(mmap2, unsigned long, addr, unsigned long, len, unsigned long, prot, unsigned long, flags, unsigned long, fd, unsigned long, pgoff)
prose: Generated microblaze syscall function sys_mmap2 taking addr, len, prot, flags, fd and pgoff, where pgoff is in units of 4096 bytes. If (pgoff & (~PAGE_MASK >> 12)) is non-zero it returns -EINVAL (that mask is zero when PAGE_SIZE is 4096, so the test then never fires). Otherwise it returns the value of ksys_mmap_pgoff(addr, len, prot, flags, fd, pgoff >> (PAGE_SHIFT - 12)) unchanged. Those are its only two returns.
note: Macro-generated function; name is the SYSCALL_DEFINE6 invocation (sys_microblaze.c:46-55). The 4096-byte-page qualification on the mask was added; old prose stated it unconditionally for the kernel PAGE_SIZE.

name: bcm63xx_set_cs_base
prose: Function bcm63xx_set_cs_base(cs, base, size) configuring the base address and size of a bcm63xx MPI chip select. Return paths: -EINVAL if cs is greater than 6 (is_valid_cs); -EINVAL if size != roundup_pow_of_two(size) (so size must be a power of two; the helper is only defined for size >= 1 and, on a 32-bit unsigned int, not above 2^31); -EINVAL if size is below 8192 or above 268435456; in each of these cases no hardware access is made. Otherwise it forms val = (base & MPI_CSBASE_BASE_MASK) | ((ilog2(size) - ilog2(8192)) << MPI_CSBASE_SIZE_SHIFT), takes bcm63xx_cs_lock with spin_lock_irqsave, writes val to MPI_CSBASE_REG(cs), releases the lock with spin_unlock_irqrestore and returns 0.
note: Contract cleared: it names roundup_pow_of_two and hardware registers (reviewer rounds all flagged the missing EINVAL in the contract; the prose already had it). Slice 35-59.

name: bcm63xx_set_cs_timing
prose: Function bcm63xx_set_cs_timing(cs, wait, setup, hold). If cs is greater than 6 it returns -EINVAL without touching the hardware. Otherwise it takes bcm63xx_cs_lock with spin_lock_irqsave, reads MPI_CSCTL_REG(cs), clears the WAIT, SETUP and HOLD fields, ORs in wait, setup and hold shifted to their field positions (the values are not masked to the field widths), writes the register back, releases the lock with spin_unlock_irqrestore and returns 0.
note: Contract cleared (hardware access and lock). Old prose accurate; added that values are shifted in without masking (cs.c:80-82). Slice 66-87.

name: bcm63xx_set_cs_param
prose: Function bcm63xx_set_cs_param(cs, params). It returns -EINVAL without touching the hardware if cs is greater than 6, or if cs is one of MPI_CS_PCMCIA_COMMON, MPI_CS_PCMCIA_ATTR or MPI_CS_PCMCIA_IO (4, 5 and 6). Otherwise it takes bcm63xx_cs_lock with spin_lock_irqsave, reads MPI_CSCTL_REG(cs), clears the DATA16, SYNCMODE, TSIZE and ENDIANSWAP masks, ORs in params as given (not masked), writes the register back, releases the lock with spin_unlock_irqrestore and returns 0.
note: Contract cleared (hardware access and lock). PCMCIA chip-select values checked in asm/mach-bcm63xx/bcm63xx_regs.h:1029-1031. Slice 94-119.

name: bcm63xx_set_cs_status
prose: Function bcm63xx_set_cs_status(cs, enable). If cs is greater than 6 it returns -EINVAL without touching the hardware. Otherwise it takes bcm63xx_cs_lock with spin_lock_irqsave, reads MPI_CSCTL_REG(cs), sets MPI_CSCTL_ENABLE_MASK if enable is non-zero and clears it if enable is zero, writes the register back, releases the lock with spin_unlock_irqrestore and returns 0.
note: Contract cleared (hardware access and lock). Slice 126-143.

name: bcm63xx_detect_flash_type
prose: Static __init function with no arguments that reports the flash type of the board from the CPU id and boot strap registers. It switches on bcm63xx_get_cpu_id(): BCM6328 reads MISC_STRAPBUS_6328_REG and returns BCM63XX_FLASH_TYPE_SERIAL if STRAPBUS_6328_BOOT_SEL_SERIAL is set, else BCM63XX_FLASH_TYPE_NAND; BCM6338, BCM6345 and BCM6348 return BCM63XX_FLASH_TYPE_PARALLEL without reading hardware; BCM3368 and BCM6358 read GPIO_STRAPBUS_REG and return PARALLEL if STRAPBUS_6358_BOOT_SEL_PARALLEL is set, else SERIAL; BCM6362 reads MISC_STRAPBUS_6362_REG and returns SERIAL if STRAPBUS_6362_BOOT_SEL_SERIAL is set, else NAND; BCM6368 reads GPIO_STRAPBUS_REG and returns NAND, SERIAL or PARALLEL when (val & STRAPBUS_6368_BOOT_SEL_MASK) equals the corresponding STRAPBUS_6368_BOOT_SEL_ value, and -EINVAL for any other value; any other CPU id returns -EINVAL. The enum values are PARALLEL 0, SERIAL 1 and NAND 2, so the results are 0, 1, 2 or -EINVAL (-22). It has no side effects beyond reading registers.
note: Contract cleared: result depends on CPU id and hardware registers. Prose was accurate; reviewers only objected to the contract omitting EINVAL. Enum values checked in asm/mach-bcm63xx/bcm63xx_dev_flash.h:6-8. Slice 58-101.

name: main
prose: Program entry of the elf2ecoff host tool, main(argc, argv): converts the 32-bit ELF executable argv[1] into an ECOFF file argv[2]. It never returns normally: every path ends in exit(). It exits with status 1 and a stderr message if argc is below 3 or above 4, or if argc is 4 and argv[3] is not "-a" (a usage message; "-a" sets addflag so 6 section headers are written instead of 3); if argv[1] cannot be opened; if reading the ELF header gives a short count; if saveRead fails (lseek, malloc or short read of the program or section headers); if a program header has a type other than PT_NULL, PT_NOTE, PT_PHDR, PT_MIPS_REGINFO, PT_MIPS_ABIFLAGS or PT_LOAD; if combining PT_LOAD pieces finds non-contiguous text or data (combine); if the text, data and bss sections are out of order or overlap; if argv[2] cannot be opened or created (open with O_WRONLY | O_CREAT, mode 0777, no truncation); if writing the file header, a.out header or section headers does not write the full size; if an intersegment gap is larger than 65536 bytes; if a write of gap zeroes returns a negative count; if copy of a segment fails (lseek, short read or short write); or if the final 4096-byte zero page is not written in full. It sorts the program headers by vaddr, builds text, data and bss from the PT_LOAD headers (a writable segment is data plus bss, others are text), then writes the ECOFF file header, the a.out header, the section headers, up to 15 bytes of zero alignment padding to a 16-byte boundary (a negative write result is an error, a short positive write is not checked), each PT_LOAD segment with non-zero p_filesz in order preceded by a zero fill of any gap with a warning, and a 4096-byte page of zeros; then it calls exit(0). The input and output descriptors are never closed explicitly, and a failure after the output file was opened may leave a partial output file.
note: Reviewer round 15 right: the alignment pad write only tests i < 0 (elf2ecoff.c slice 46-50), so a short write is not an error; the old prose said any short write exits. Missing exits added: saveRead failures and non-contiguous combine (lines 102-117, 133-155). The slice cut the head, so argument handling, ELF header read and the program-header loop were read from the real file lines 267-505. Note: after exit(1) at slice line 14 the following loop is unreachable.

name: __cvmx_get_mode_octeon2
prose: Static function __cvmx_get_mode_octeon2(interface) returning the interface mode for an Octeon II model; it only reads CSRs and has no side effects. In order: (1) on CN68XX it returns __cvmx_get_mode_cn68xx(interface); (2) interface 2 returns CVMX_HELPER_INTERFACE_MODE_NPI and interface 3 returns CVMX_HELPER_INTERFACE_MODE_LOOP, for any model reaching this point; (3) CN63XX interfaces 4 and 5 and CN66XX interfaces 4 to 7 return DISABLED; (4) on CN66XX: interface 0 reads CVMX_MIO_QLMX_CFG(2), interface 1 reads CVMX_MIO_QLMX_CFG(1), any other interface returns DISABLED; then DISABLED if qlm_spd is 15, SGMII if qlm_cfg is 9, XAUI if qlm_cfg is 11, DISABLED otherwise (this block always returns); (5) on CN61XX: interface 0 reads CVMX_MIO_QLMX_CFG(2) and interface 1 reads CVMX_MIO_QLMX_CFG(0), each returning SGMII for qlm_cfg 2, XAUI for qlm_cfg 3 and DISABLED otherwise; CN61XX interfaces other than 0 and 1 (and not 2 or 3, already handled in (2)) leave this block and continue to the code below; (6) on CNF71XX: interface 0 returns SGMII when CVMX_MIO_QLMX_CFG(0) has qlm_cfg 2, and every other case (including interface 0 with another value, and every interface other than 2 and 3, which were handled in (2)) returns DISABLED; (7) CN63XX interface 1 returns DISABLED; (8) otherwise it reads CVMX_GMXX_INF_MODE(interface): on CN63XX it returns SGMII for mode 0, XAUI for mode 1 and DISABLED for other modes; on other models it returns DISABLED if the en bit is clear, else GMII if the type bit is set and RGMII if clear.
note: Reviewer rounds 1, 2 and 15 point at exceptions to old wording: round 1 right (CN68XX delegates before the interface 2/3 tests, so those only apply to other models; the old text said this but in confusing order), round 2 wrong (old prose already said CNF71XX 2 and 3 are not DISABLED), round 15 right (old text implied CN61XX interfaces 2 and 3 fall through; they return NPI/LOOP at lines 157-161). Slice 150-244.

name: cvmx_l2c_get_hw_way_partition
prose: Function with no arguments that reads the hardware L2 way partition register. If OCTEON_IS_MODEL(OCTEON_CN63XX) it returns cvmx_read_csr(CVMX_L2C_WPAR_IOBX(0)) & 0xffff (a value 0 to 65535); otherwise it returns cvmx_read_csr(CVMX_L2C_SPAR4) & 0xFF (a value 0 to 255). It has no side effects other than the CSR read and takes no lock.
note: Contract cleared: it reads a model-dependent hardware register (reviewers rounds 1 and 15 both said the formal contract was weaker than the prose). Prose was accurate; slice 161-167. The word global was dropped as unsupported.

name: cvmx_l2c_get_cache_size_bytes
prose: Function with no arguments returning cvmx_l2c_get_num_sets() * cvmx_l2c_get_num_assoc() * CVMX_CACHE_LINE_SIZE (128), the L2 cache size in bytes. The set count is 1 shifted by cvmx_l2c_get_set_bits(), which depends on the Octeon model (128 to 2048 sets; an unsupported model prints a message and is treated as 2048 sets). The associativity depends on the model (4, 8 or 16 ways; unsupported models are treated as 8) reduced by the fuse bits: on CN63XX to 12, 8 or 4 ways, on other models divided by 2 or 4. Over all models and fuse settings the value is one of 32768, 65536, 131072, 262144, 524288, 1048576, 1572864 or 2097152. It reads fuse CSRs and may print through cvmx_dprintf, but changes no state.
note: Contract cleared: it depends on the model and fuse CSRs. Reviewers rounds 1, 2 and 15 are wrong about the old prose: it already listed 32768 as a possible value and already stated the sets * associativity * line size formula; I verified the possible values by enumerating every model branch of cvmx_l2c_get_set_bits / cvmx_l2c_get_num_assoc (cvmx-l2c.c, callee definitions before line 761).

name: cvmx_spi_reset_cb
prose: Function cvmx_spi_reset_cb(interface, mode) that resets an Octeon SPI4 interface; mode is not used. interface is used as the register index for CSRs (a valid SPI interface is 0 or 1; it is not checked). It busy-waits with __delay for about 10 ms, then 100 ms, then 100 ms (cpu clock based). Steps: it saves SPXX_INT_MSK and STXX_INT_MSK and writes 0 to both; clears SRXX_COM_CTL and STXX_COM_CTL; writes SPXX_CLK_CTL with runbist = 1, waits 10 ms, reads SPXX_BIST_STAT and prints a debug message for each of stat0, stat1 and stat2 that is set (BIST failures are only printed, not returned); writes 32 entries (index 0 to 31) of SRXX_SPI4_CALX and STXX_SPI4_CALX as zero with oddpar = 1; writes back the value read from SPXX_INT_REG and STXX_INT_REG (clearing pending bits) and restores the two saved interrupt masks; writes SPXX_CLK_CTL with clkdly = 0x10, statrcv = 1 and the other fields 0, waits 100 ms; sets srxdlck = 1 and rewrites SPXX_CLK_CTL, waits 100 ms; writes SPXX_TRN4_CTL with trntest = 0, jitter = 1, clr_boot = 1, set_boot = 0, maxdist = 3 on CN58XX and 8 otherwise, macro_en = 1 and mux_en = 1 (the other fields of that register value come from an uninitialised local variable); writes SPXX_DBG_DESKEW_CTL as 0; and returns 0. The only return is 0 at the end; there is no error return.
note: Contract cleared (hardware side effects). Original-rejection claim (no return statement; BIST failures not returned) is wrong about the return: cvmx-spi.c ends with return 0 (real file line ~290), but right that BIST failures are only printed. Slice cut the tail; read the rest from the real file lines 254-292. Old prose omitted the uninitialised fields of spxx_trn4_ctl.

name: csum_tcpudp_nofold
prose: Static inline function csum_tcpudp_nofold(saddr, daddr, len, proto, isum) returning the unfolded 32-bit pseudo-header checksum sum; it reads no memory and has no side effects. It adds daddr, saddr, (proto + len) and isum as unsigned long values; the (proto + len) term is cast to a signed 32-bit value first (the code assumes its sign bit is clear) and is shifted left by 8 on little-endian builds, not shifted on big-endian builds. On 32-bit builds each addition adds the carry back in (end-around carry); on 64-bit builds the 64-bit total is folded to 32 bits by adding its two 32-bit halves with the carry added back. The result is therefore the ones-complement style sum of the terms: equal to the integer total modulo 4294967295, except that a non-zero total that is a multiple of 4294967295 gives 4294967295; and the result is 0 only when all inputs contribute zero. The result is only correct when the shifted (proto + len) term fits the width of unsigned long, i.e. len + proto < 16777216 on 32-bit little-endian builds (larger on 64-bit builds); the build fails (BUILD_BUG) if neither CONFIG_32BIT nor CONFIG_64BIT is set.
note: Checked against the slice: the structure (32-bit: carry after each add; 64-bit: fold of halves, lines 157-167) matches the old prose. Precondition reworded: the 2^24 limit is a 32-bit LE limit, 64-bit builds hold the shifted term in 64 bits. Reviewer round 1 only concerned the contract, which is empty here.

name: set_dma_count
prose: Static inline function set_dma_count(dmanr, count) that programs the transfer count of DMA channel dmanr; it returns nothing and assumes the DMA controller flip-flop is clear (per the comment above it). It first decrements count (so count 0 becomes 0xffffffff). If dmanr <= 3 it writes count & 0xff and then (count >> 8) & 0xff with dma_outb to port ((dmanr & 3) << 1) + 1 + IO_DMA1_BASE. Otherwise (dmanr 4 to 7) it writes (count >> 1) & 0xff and then (count >> 9) & 0xff to port ((dmanr & 3) << 2) + 2 + IO_DMA2_BASE. Only the low 16 bits of the decremented count (of count >> 1 for channels above 3) are written, so counts larger than 64K for channels 0-3, or 128K above, are truncated; the comment states that count is in bytes and must be even for channels 5-7, but the code halves it for every channel above 3, including channel 4.
note: Reviewer round 1 right that the code halves count for all dmanr > 3 (the old prose said channels above 3 but the comment text says 5-7; both are kept visible now). Round 15 right that larger counts are truncated (set_dma_count slice lines 12-19); added. Slice 10-20.

name: get_dma_residue
prose: Static inline function get_dma_residue(dmanr) returning the number of bytes left for DMA channel dmanr; it assumes the DMA flip-flop is clear. It selects the port ((dmanr & 3) << 1) + 1 + IO_DMA1_BASE for dmanr <= 3, else ((dmanr & 3) << 2) + 2 + IO_DMA2_BASE. It reads the port once for the low byte and again for the high byte, forming an unsigned short count = (1 + low byte + (high byte << 8)) with 16-bit wraparound. It returns count for dmanr <= 3 and count << 1 (an int up to 131070) for dmanr > 3. The comment says the value is expected to be 0 after a completed transfer, that it may be 1 if the channel has not been used, and that reading during a transfer gives unpredictable results; none of these is enforced by the code. It writes no memory and takes no lock.
note: Reviewer round 15 right: the code does not guarantee 1 for an unused channel; that is only the comment may-return statement, and the old prose asserted it. Slice 31-43.

name: BUILDIO_IOPORT(b, u8)
prose: Generated function _outb(val, port) (static inline, from __BUILD_IOPORT_SINGLE(_, b, u8, 1, 0) via BUILDIO_IOPORT(b, u8); an identical function __mem_outb is generated by the same invocation). It issues iobarrier_rw() (the barrier flag is 1), computes the address __swizzle_addr_b(mips_io_port_base + port), converts val with the platform _ioswabb macro (defined by the platform mangle-port.h or io.h; it may swap or leave the value unchanged) and stores the result through that volatile address. It returns nothing; the destination must be a mapped I/O address.
note: Macro-generated (mips/include/asm/io.h:1-41 and 67-73). Old prose said the value is byte-swapped; whether it is swapped is platform dependent (ioswab/swizzle are per-machine macros), so it was weakened.

name: BUILDIO_IOPORT(b, u8)
prose: Generated function _inb(port) (static inline, from __BUILD_IOPORT_SINGLE(_, b, u8, 1, 0) via BUILDIO_IOPORT(b, u8); an identical __mem_inb is generated by the same invocation). It computes the address __swizzle_addr_b(mips_io_port_base + port), issues iobarrier_rw(), reads the byte through the volatile address, calls rmb() (the relax flag is 0), and returns the value passed through the platform _ioswabb macro (which may or may not change it).
note: Macro-generated (io.h:23-41, instantiated at 71). Order of operations matches the slice: address, barrier, load, rmb, return. Swap wording weakened as for _outb.

name: BUILDIO_IOPORT(l, u32)
prose: Generated function _inl(port) (static inline, from __BUILD_IOPORT_SINGLE(_, l, u32, 1, 0) via BUILDIO_IOPORT(l, u32); an identical __mem_inl is generated by the same invocation). It computes the address __swizzle_addr_l(mips_io_port_base + port), issues iobarrier_rw(), reads a 32-bit value through the volatile address, calls rmb(), and returns the value passed through the platform _ioswabl macro (which may swap bytes or leave it unchanged depending on the platform and CONFIG_SWAP_IO_SPACE).

name: BUILDSTRING(b, u8)
prose: Generated function writesb(mem, addr, count) (static inline, from __BUILD_MEMORY_STRING(b, u8)). It loops count times (count is an unsigned int; with count 0 nothing happens), each time calling __mem_writeb(*__addr, mem) for the next source byte and then advancing the source pointer; the destination address mem is not advanced, so all bytes go to the same I/O address. It reads count bytes from addr and returns nothing.

name: BUILDSTRING(l, u32)

It loops count times (count is an unsigned int; with count 0 nothing happens), each time storing the result of __mem_readl(mem) into the current 32-bit element at addr and advancing addr by one element; mem is not advanced, so every read is from the same I/O address. It writes count 32-bit words at addr and returns nothing.

name: BUILDSTRING(l, u32)
prose: Generated function insl(port, addr, count) (static inline, from __BUILD_IOPORT_STRING(l, u32)). It loops count times (count is an unsigned int; with count 0 nothing happens), each time storing the result of __mem_inl(port) into the current 32-bit element at addr and advancing addr by one element; the port is not advanced. It writes count 32-bit words at addr and returns nothing.
note: Macro-generated (io.h:153-162, instantiated at 171).

name: BUILDSTRING(l, u32)
prose: Generated function outsl(port, addr, count) (static inline, from __BUILD_IOPORT_STRING(l, u32)). It loops count times (count is an unsigned int; with count 0 nothing happens), each time calling __mem_outl(*__addr, port) with the next 32-bit source element and advancing the source pointer; the port is not advanced. It reads count 32-bit words from addr and returns nothing.

name: alchemy_gpio_direction_input
prose: Static inline function alchemy_gpio_direction_input(gpio) that returns the result of one of two helpers: alchemy_gpio2_direction_input(gpio) if gpio >= ALCHEMY_GPIO2_BASE, otherwise alchemy_gpio1_direction_input(gpio). The GPIO1 helper writes the mask 1 << (gpio - ALCHEMY_GPIO1_BASE) to AU1000_SYS_TRIOUTCLR with alchemy_wrsys and returns 0, without disabling local interrupts. The GPIO2 helper disables local interrupts with local_irq_save, calls __alchemy_gpio2_mod_dir(gpio, 0) and restores interrupts with local_irq_restore, then returns 0. The returned value is 0 in both cases; no range check is made on gpio.
note: Reviewer round 15 right: only the GPIO2 path disables local interrupts (gpio-au1000.h:231-236 vs 314-321); old prose claimed both paths do. Callee definitions read in the real file (slice shows only the wrapper, lines 216-221).

name: alchemy_gpio_direction_output
prose: Static inline function alchemy_gpio_direction_output(gpio, v) that returns the result of one of two helpers: alchemy_gpio2_direction_output(gpio, v) if gpio >= ALCHEMY_GPIO2_BASE, otherwise alchemy_gpio1_direction_output(gpio, v). The GPIO1 helper only calls alchemy_gpio1_set_value(gpio, v) (the hardware switches the pin to output when a set-value register is accessed) and returns 0, without disabling local interrupts. The GPIO2 helper calls alchemy_gpio2_set_value(gpio, v), then disables local interrupts with local_irq_save, calls __alchemy_gpio2_mod_dir(gpio, 1), restores interrupts, and returns 0. The returned value is 0 in both cases; no range check is made on gpio.
note: Reviewer round 15 right (GPIO1 path does not disable interrupts, gpio-au1000.h:238-245 vs 323-331); the old prose also said the output value is set first and then the direction, which is true for GPIO2 and for GPIO1 is the single set-value call.

name: mips_cm_l2sync
prose: Static inline function with no arguments that performs an L2-only sync. If mips_cm_has_l2sync() is false it returns -ENODEV without writing anything. Otherwise it writes 0 to mips_cm_l2sync_base with writel and returns 0. It takes no lock.
note: The old prose gave the value of ENODEV as -11; the correct Linux value of ENODEV is 19 (EAGAIN is 11), so the number was removed and the symbolic name kept (mips-cm.h slice 137-144).

name: cvmx_cmd_queue_write3
prose: Static inline function cvmx_cmd_queue_write3(queue_id, use_locking, cmd1, cmd2, cmd3) that appends three 64-bit command words to a hardware command queue. qptr is __cvmx_cmd_queue_get_state(queue_id). If use_locking is non-zero it takes the queue lock itself with __cvmx_cmd_queue_lock at the start, and every return below releases it with __cvmx_cmd_queue_unlock when use_locking is non-zero. Returns: (1) CVMX_CMD_QUEUE_FULL, with nothing written, if CVMX_CMD_QUEUE_ENABLE_MAX_DEPTH is enabled, qptr->max_depth is non-zero and cvmx_cmd_queue_length(queue_id) is greater than max_depth; (2) if qptr->index + 3 < qptr->pool_size_m1 the three words are stored at the current index of the current buffer, the index is advanced by 3, and it returns CVMX_CMD_QUEUE_SUCCESS; (3) otherwise it allocates a new buffer with cvmx_fpa_alloc(qptr->fpa_pool) and returns CVMX_CMD_QUEUE_NO_MEMORY, with nothing written, if that returns NULL; else it writes as many of cmd1..cmd3 as fit in the remaining space of the current buffer, stores the physical address of the new buffer as the link word after them, makes the new buffer current with index 0, writes the remaining command words at its start (advancing index accordingly), and returns CVMX_CMD_QUEUE_SUCCESS.
note: The listed name cvmx_cmd_queue_post_multi_3 does not exist: the slice cut the head and the function is cvmx_cmd_queue_write3 (cvmx-cmd-queue.h:~519-612). Old prose wrong on the precondition: the function takes the lock itself when use_locking is set (it does not require the caller to hold it). Slice 6-13 and 19-80 checked for returns.

name: __BUILD_BLAST_CACHE(d, dcache, Index_Writeback_Inv_D, Hit_Writeback_Inv_D, 32, )
prose: Generated function blast_dcache32() (static inline, from __BUILD_BLAST_CACHE with line size 32). It writes back and invalidates the whole primary data cache by index. With start = INDEX_BASE, end = start + current_cpu_data.dcache.waysize, ws_inc = 1 << dcache.waybit and ws_end = dcache.ways << dcache.waybit, it loops ws from 0 to ws_end in steps of ws_inc and, for each ws, addr from start to end in steps of 1024 bytes (32 lines of 32 bytes); each step issues 32 Index_Writeback_Inv_D cache operations at (addr | ws) + k * 32 for k = 0 to 31. name: gt641xx_timer0_state
prose: Function with no arguments that starts timer 0 if it is not already counting. It reads GT_TC0_OFS with GT_READ. If the value is non-zero it returns 0 and performs no write. Otherwise it writes gt641xx_base_clock / HZ to GT_TC0_OFS with GT_WRITE, then writes GT_TC_CONTROL_ENTC0_MSK to GT_TC_CONTROL_OFS with GT_WRITE (a full-register write of that value), and returns 1. The only returns are 0 and 1.
note: Reviewer round 15 right: the old text said it touches no register on the 0 path, but it reads GT_TC0_OFS (cevt-gt641xx.c slice line 26); the prose now says no write is made. Also removed the inference that other control bits are cleared (it is only stated that the write value is the enable mask). Slice 24-33.

name: cpu_get_msa_id
prose: Static inline function with no arguments that reads the MSA implementation register. It saves the CP0 Status register, calls __enable_fpu(FPU_64BIT), calls enable_msa() (which sets the Config5.MSAEn bit only if cpu_has_msa), reads read_msa_ir() into msa_id, calls disable_msa() (which clears Config5.MSAEn only if cpu_has_msa), writes the saved value back to CP0 Status, and returns msa_id. Status is therefore restored to its entry value, but the MSA enable bit in Config5 is cleared by disable_msa() whether or not it was set on entry. The function does not itself check that the CPU has MSA before reading the register, so it is meant to be called on a CPU known to have it.
note: Reviewer round 2 is wrong: MSA is not left as it was; disable_msa() explicitly clears Config5.MSAEn (asm/msa.h:105-111) and the Status restore does not affect Config5, so the old prose (state left exactly as on entry) was wrong, which round 1 hinted. Round 15 is right that there is no guard for CPUs without MSA, and the claim that the read value is unspecified there was unsupported. Slice 43-54.

name: SYSCALL_DEFINE1(32_personality, unsigned long, personality)
prose: Generated MIPS o32 syscall function sys_32_personality taking personality. It sets p = personality & 0xffffffff. If the current task personality has PER_MASK bits equal to PER_LINUX32 and p has PER_MASK bits equal to PER_LINUX, it replaces the PER_MASK bits of p with PER_LINUX32. It then calls sys_personality(p) and, if the result is not -1 and its PER_MASK bits equal PER_LINUX32, replaces the PER_MASK bits of the result with PER_LINUX. It returns that result; a result of -1 from sys_personality is returned unchanged. It takes no lock itself.
note: Macro-generated (linux32.c:89-101). Old prose said it returns -1 on failure; the code only passes through a -1 returned by sys_personality, and personality(x) here is the macro x & PER_MASK.
